problem_text:
A logistics firm must coordinate a supply chain circuit connecting twelve distribution hubs across a regional network.  
The geographical positions of these hubs are specified by the following grid coordinates:  

Hub Alpha: (83,17)  
Hub Beta: (15,88)  
Hub Gamma: (169,108)  
Hub Delta: (34,55)  
Hub Epsilon: (114,111)  
Hub Zeta: (36,91)  
Hub Eta: (79,45)  
Hub Theta: (166,84)  
Hub Iota: (186,191)  
Hub Kappa: (104,97)  
Hub Lambda: (2,104)  
Hub Mu: (67,136)

Due to infrastructure limitations, no direct route exists between Hub Alpha and Hub Beta.  
Furthermore, operational regulations require that exactly one of two critical corridors be incorporated into the circuit: either the link between Beta and Gamma, or the link between Gamma and Delta.  

The objective is to determine the minimal total travel distance for a closed loop that visits every hub precisely once and returns to the point of origin.
